headline: Keep {arm:September}. Both candidates increase cost and degrade character adherence.
lede: {arm:September} delivers the highest adherence at {pass_rate.September|pct} while costing {cost_per_1k.September|usd} compared to over {cost_per_1k.1017|usd} for both alternatives. A switch would require a candidate that reduces spend without regressing persona adherence.

slots.text: Retain {arm:September} in production. It maintains {pass_rate.September|pct} pass rate at {cost_per_1k.September|usd}.

{arm:1017} drops adherence by {reading.1017.change|abs|pts} points while increasing cost to {cost_per_1k.1017|usd}. {arm:qwen3.8-flash} drops adherence by {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points ({reading.qwen3.8-flash.interval|interval} points) and raises cost to {cost_per_1k.qwen3.8-flash|usd}.

The weakest margin is {weakest.arm} with {weakest.value|pts} points against {weakest.threshold|pts} points on {weakest.criterion} ({weakest.margin} points gap). Note reasoning ratio differed across models ({reasoning_ratio.September|pct} on {arm:September} vs {reasoning_ratio.1017|pct} on {arm:1017}), and {arm:qwen3.8-flash} had two degraded harness runs. Prior insight that {arm:qwen3.8-flash} lowers production costs is contradicted.
Test lighter prompt variants or lower reasoning budgets on {arm:September} to reduce cost without sacrificing persona adherence.
